name: Incorrect Calculation of Buffer Size
principle: The code calculates an allocation size that is smaller or otherwise different from the bytes later required. The resulting buffer can be overrun or read past, causing crash, memory disclosure, memory modification, or code execution.
detection_signals: malloc/calloc/realloc/alloca/new[] size argument uses user-controlled arithmetic without overflow checks
malloc(strlen(x)) or new char[strlen(x)] followed by strcpy/strcat/sprintf writing a NUL terminator
allocation uses element count without * sizeof(element_type) before indexing elements
allocation expression omits +1 or sentinel slot but later writes buf[n]=0, NULL, or terminator
encoding/escaping/conversion output buffer uses fixed multiplier smaller than maximum expansion, e.g. HTML '&' to '&'
signed int/long length is checked only for upper bound then cast or passed to size_t allocation
allocation uses sizeof(pointer) where sizeof(*pointer) or sizeof(type) is required
negative_signals: code validates length >= 0 and length <= maximum before allocation
allocation includes terminator or sentinel, e.g. strlen(s)+1 or (n+1)*sizeof(T)
allocation uses sizeof *ptr or sizeof(T) consistently with element writes
conversion buffer is sized for documented worst-case expansion
Java code uses arrays/StringBuilder without manual byte-size arithmetic and catches impossible negative sizes by validation
false_defense_traps: Replacing strcpy with strncpy while keeping the undersized allocation
Checking only maximum length but not negative signed lengths
Relying on client-side length validation without server-side revalidation
Using ASLR/NX/canaries/FORTIFY_SOURCE as the only fix
Assuming sizeof(ptr) equals the pointed-to object size
verification_focus: Does the allocation-size expression exactly cover element size, count, sentinel, worst-case expansion, sign, and overflow before any write/read uses the buffer?

consequence_chains.trigger: allocated buffer is smaller than later memory operation requires
consequence_chains.consequence: out-of-bounds read/write, crash, memory disclosure, memory modification, or code execution

consequence_chains.trigger: calculation omits one byte or one element for a terminator/sentinel
multiplication or addition wraps before allocation
negative signed length is converted to unsigned allocation size
consequence_chains.consequence: incorrect allocation size, allocation failure, or later memory error

patch_principle: Compute allocation in bytes with the correct element type and include all terminators or sentinels.
Validate numeric inputs for minimum and maximum bounds before allocation.
Use checked integer arithmetic for size additions and multiplications.
For transformations or encodings, allocate for the maximum possible output expansion.
Prefer vetted containers or safe allocation helpers that track size.
